paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the leaders asked Jesus a question they didn't really want answered. They asked, "By what authority are You doing these things?" (Mark 11:28), but when He asked about John's baptism, they only worried about what the people would think of them. They said, "We do not know," (Mark 11:33), and I think they knew a lot more than they let on. You can't honestly ask about Jesus' authority while you're guarding your own spot.

Then Jesus tells about a man who planted a vineyard and rented it to tenants. The owner kept sending people, and in the end he sent "one beloved son" (Mark 12:6), saying, "They will respect my son." The tenants saw the heir and wanted the inheritance for themselves. Jesus tells it so the leaders can see themselves in it, and verse 12 says they knew He had spoken this parable against them.

So what does that mean for you, baker? Jesus is the stone the builders rejected, and Scripture says it "has become the cornerstone. This is from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes" (Mark 12:10-11). People can push Him out, and He still ends up in the most important spot. Don't ask about Him just to protect your own place. Ask because you want the answer, and then let Him have the spot that is already His.
